# A11y Plan — Amendments

_Append-only v3 changelog for `a11y-plan.md`. The plan **body** holds current truth only; this sidecar holds the amendment **history** (decisions, re-audits, harness repairs, re-baselines). Where an amendment carried current-truth substance, that substance was folded into the plan body and the entry below points to where it now lives._

_Format per entry: `## {date} — {title}` with **Section** / **Change** / **Why** / **Marker**._

## 2026-05-02 — Initial a11y plan generated by `/andromeda-a11y`
**Section:** §1 Scope, §3 Harness Contract, §6 Visual Verification, §9 CI, §11 Anti-Patterns — every tool pick, version, and the tier decision below is current truth in those sections; only the selection *rationale* is history kept here.
**Change:** First generation of the plan. A11y tier Standard (1) → WCAG 2.1 AA (~50 SCs) with a motion-sensitive AAA escalation (SC 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions). Tool stack:
- A11y testing: `@axe-core/playwright` 4.11.x + Lighthouse 12.x + pa11y 9.x
- Focus management: focus-trap-react 12.x + tabbable 6.4.x
- ARIA components: React Aria Components 1.17.x OR Headless UI 2.2.x (never both)
- Motion / reduced-motion: Tailwind v4 `motion-reduce:` / `motion-safe:` variants + `motion/react` 12.x `useReducedMotion`
- Contrast: axe-core color-contrast rule + colorjs.io 0.6.x token-based checker
**Why:** axe-core covers ~50 WCAG 2.1 AA SCs via tagged rules and piggybacks on the tests' Playwright 5-command E2E harness; Lighthouse 12 adds the prefers-reduced-motion (SC 2.3.3 AAA) + focus-visible (SC 2.4.7) audits; pa11y 9 gives a parallel rule matrix. focus-trap-react handles modal entry/exit/escape-close/focus-restore (SC 2.1.2 / SC 2.4.3); tabbable computes the expected Tab order for assertions. React Aria covers the Dialog / RadioGroup / Slider / Switch / ComboBox / Menu / Tabs / Form patterns of P2–P7 (Headless UI is lighter for Tailwind-tight builds); never mix the two. colorjs.io implements the WCAG 2.1 contrast algorithm and reads design tokens verbatim via `getComputedStyle`. Tier justified by 2 primary UI surfaces (desktop-webview + desktop-native tray), 8 assertable entities, 7 must-be-accessible flows (P1–P7), tests + obs both Standard, security Minimal (no regulated-compliance trigger). No open questions deferred.
**Ref:** NOT DERIVED

## 2026-06-10 — Chunk #99 tag gate: v0.2.0 full re-audit + harness repair + surface extension + baseline re-established
**Section:** §1 Scope (surface set + SC 1.4.13 applicability), §3 Harness Contract (wiring + regression baseline), §6 / §11 (remediation patterns), §9 CI (regression gate restored). See **Folded into body** below for where the current-truth substance now lives.
**Change:**
- Surface set P1–P7 → P1–P12 (§1 note after the Critical paths table): NEW p8 findings dropdown, p9 diagnostic report modal, p10 diagnostics view, p11 constellation semantics, p12 export preview; NEW `keyboard-focus/widget-and-modals.spec.ts`; p5 + reduced-motion specs updated to the redesigned (post-chunk-#89/#90/#91) widget.
- New §3 "Harness wiring & conventions" subsection: taurpc 0.7 invokes `TauRPC__<router.path>` (mock regex `/^TauRPC__([\w.]+)$/`, not `plugin:taurpc|<path>`); window label read from `__TAURI_INTERNALS__.metadata.currentWebview.label`; `plugin:event|listen` handler; helpers `mock-tauri.ts` / `v02-fixtures.ts` / `static-server.mjs` (`http-server` with `-P` SPA fallback — TanStack Router uses browser history, `/#/route` never routed) / `pa11y/run-pa11y.mjs`; real route paths (incl. `/diagnostics`) in pa11y/Lighthouse configs; one devDep `http-server`; standing rule: add an axe spec per new route/modal; `npx playwright test --list` health check.
- Regression baseline `baselines/a11y-violations-summary.json` regenerated 2026-06-09 from a clean full-chain pass — 6 informational lighthouse-score tuples, 0 violation tuples; the v0.2.0 regression baseline (§9 gate restored).
- §1 "SCs not applicable": SC 1.4.13 does not apply to the header connection-dot tooltip (non-interactive `role="img"` summary with an `aria-hidden` decorative tooltip).
- No tooling-stack change (axe / Lighthouse / pa11y retained).
**Why:** The Playwright a11y suite had been silently dead since session 64 (a list-time import failure: stale `../helpers/mock-tauri` import) behind four infrastructure bugs masking all route-level audits, so the §9 violation-JSON regression gate guarded nothing. The v0.2.0 tag gate ran `cargo xtask test:a11y`; the repair restores the gate and extends machine-verifiable WCAG 2.1 AA + SC 2.3.3 AAA evidence to every v0.2.0 surface. ~10 violations were fixed in-chunk — SC 2.5.8 target-size (WindowControls min 24px); SC 1.4.3 / 1.4.11 contrast (tertiary → secondary text; severity text → `text-primary` + severity-colored borders); svg-img-alt; no dangling `aria-controls` (TabNav emits it only when the tab is active AND its route is current, via `activeIsCurrentRoute`); focus-toggled SkipToMain clip — all applications of rules already current in §6 / §11, so no new body rule. The SC 1.4.13 determination is recorded so future audits do not re-flag it. a11y-plan §10 hard gates + §11 machine-verifiable-evidence invariant (tier Standard) win over the stale v0.1.0 surface enumeration.
**Ref:** NOT DERIVED

## 2026-06-30-widget-to-dashboard-navigation — P5 button accessible name: "Expand to dashboard" → "Toggle dashboard"
**Section:** §1 Critical Paths (P5 row).
**Change:** The compact-widget's dashboard-navigation affordance is `<button aria-label="Toggle dashboard">` (opens the dashboard if hidden / hides it if visible; the glance widget always stays visible) — was `<button aria-label="Expand to dashboard">` (expand-and-hide). P5 row's button label + focus-management note updated: the toggle never hides the widget; the same handler is bound to Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+P in both windows.
**Why:** Live dogfood (2026-06-30) showed the planned expand-and-hide stranded the user with no way back to the widget; reframed to a toggle that keeps the widget always visible, so the accessible name changed and the P5 body's label was stale (P-066).
**Ref:** NOT DERIVED

## 2026-07-10-incidents-floating-window-disclosure — Findings + Report window focus order + cross-window restoration
**Section:** §5 Keyboard Navigation (Focus order per layout + Focus restoration)
**Change:**
- Focus order for the `findings` window: opened via FindingsCounter `aria-haspopup="dialog"`; Tab rows → mark-all-read; Esc/blur/mark-all-read dismiss + cross-window focus restore to the badge; row-select opens the report window.
- Focus order for the `report` window: `role="dialog"` fill-variant; Esc/✕ closes + cross-window focus restore to findings.
- Focus-restoration bullet: these windows restore focus across windows via Tauri events, not focus-trap-react.
**Why:** FindingsWindow + ReportWindow are separate always-on-top Tauri windows with cross-window focus/Esc restore; §5 documented only in-document layouts and described restoration via focus-trap-react `returnFocusOnDeactivate`, which cannot cross windows.
**Ref:** NOT DERIVED

## 2026-08-23-webview-self-verify — P5 tray affordance renamed to the shipped controls
**Section:** §1 A11y Scope Summary → Critical paths, P5 row · §5 Keyboard Navigation → compact-widget focus order
**Change:** Was `button[aria-label="Minimize to tray"]`; now the two controls the app ships — `button[aria-label="Minimize"]` and `button[aria-label="Close to tray"]` (the titlebar ✕ that hides the widget to the tray; Esc also triggers it). §5's single "minimize button" split into the same pair. P5's existing SC coverage (2.1.1 / 2.1.2 / 2.4.3 / 2.4.7 / 4.1.2) now applies to both.
**Why:** `"Minimize to tray"` measured at zero occurrences anywhere in the codebase; the live leg pressed the real `Close to tray` control and observed the widget transition to hidden. A P5 element named in the plan but absent from the product left the two real controls with no §5–§7 coverage anchor, and §5 restated the claim, so a single-site apply would have left it standing.
**Ref:** NOT DERIVED

## 2026-08-23-a11y-verification — Traces semantics land, and the NOT-SHIPPED claim is retracted as measurement-disproved (7 sites)
**Section:** §1 A11y Scope Summary → Critical paths P1 row · §1 Critical paths P4 row · §1 Surface set extension · §3 Harness wiring → Adding a surface · §5 Keyboard Navigation → full-dashboard-traces focus order · §7 Screen Reader Support → Landmark roles · §11 A11y Anti-Patterns → Keyboard
**Change:** Retracted the REQUIRED-but-NOT-SHIPPED claim for `region[aria-label="Telemetry traces chart"]` + the trace-list `table` role — false on both halves: the trace list was always a native `<table>` (implicit ARIA role intact, no `display:` override), and the region lives on the WebGPU canvas wrapper (`ConstellationCanvas.tsx`, a named `<section>`), not `TraceTable.tsx`. Landed: the STABLE literal landmark name + an `aria-describedby` visually-hidden aggregate summary (`data-testid="constellation-summary"`, lifecycle counts + findings tally only — no service name reaches the accessible tree), and ROW-level keyboard traversal (roving `tabindex`, Up/Down/Home/End/Enter/Esc, `--border-focus` on `:focus-visible`).
- §1 P1 + §5 state the row-level contract; the "cell navigation not assertable" premise retired.
- §1 P4 drops its NOT-SHIPPED note; the re-poll preserves row focus (P-081).
- §7 moves the region into the landmark inventory; `role="status"` recorded as a deliberate, reversible omission.
- §1 Surface set + §3 standing rule: P1–P12 → P1–P14 (p13 empty states, p14 Investigate states); new `__mockReject` / `__mockDelayMs` mock sentinels + the populated-fixture requirement.
- §11 keyboard ban narrowed from "nested focusables" to nested TAB STOPS, with an explicit grid-lite carve-out.
**Why:** This entry was the named owner and discharged its obligation; the impl was correct and only the docs were wrong (routine APPLY). The §11 narrowing was resolved with the operator: left flat, the ban prohibited the ARIA APG grid pattern shipped here, which REDUCES tab stops (one row vs one row + N Investigate buttons). Standing lesson: the earlier measurement checked the wrong file and reported an absence for a role that was present — verify a claimed absence against the component that actually owns the surface.
**Supersedes:** 2026-08-23-integration-ux-e2e-test — Traces surface semantics recorded as REQUIRED-but-NOT-SHIPPED (4 sites)
**Ref:** NOT DERIVED

## 2026-10-10-no-ci-step-reads-nothing — the regression baseline is the tree's; an absent baseline fails
**Section:** §3 → CI integration (key file: Pipeline integration, Per-PR regression detection, CI gate) · §3 → Harness wiring & conventions (key file: Regression baseline) · §1 CI Integration (the CI gate list) · §9 CI Integration (the E2E row) · §10 (Zero new violations per PR) · §11 (the per-PR diff ban)
**Change:**
- Per-PR regression detection: was "download base-branch `a11y-violations-summary.json` via `actions/download-artifact` (name `a11y-violations-base`)" and a `jq`-style filter; now the baseline is the file committed in the tree, `pulse-app/ui/tests-a11y/baselines/a11y-violations-summary.json`, nothing is downloaded, and `tests-a11y/regression-detector.mjs` (the last leg of `npm run test:a11y`) compares by the tuple key `{surface, wcag_criterion, selector, severity, violation_type}` and writes `tests-a11y/regression-set.json`.
- An absent baseline: was compared as an empty set; now exit 1 with `regression-detector: baseline not found at {path}`, pinned by `a11y_regression_baseline_is_committed_in_the_tree` and `a11y_regression_detector_fails_when_its_baseline_is_absent`.
- Pipeline integration: the `a11y` job's order loses the PR-only `a11y-violations-base` download; its two uploads fail their step when they find no file.
- Both CI gate lists gain one condition: the regression leg finds a tuple the committed baseline lacks, or the baseline file is absent.
- §9 E2E row: was "PR comment with new violations vs base branch"; now a new tuple fails the job and no step posts a pull-request comment.
- §10: was "vs base branch. Per-PR diff detection via artifact comparison"; now vs the tree baseline, no artifact compared.
- §11: the ban stands; "vs base branch" is now "vs the baseline committed in the tree", with "and on an absent baseline".
**Why:** The download never had a producer in any workflow and the comparison read the tree file all along. The operator ruled that a baseline committed in the tree at the commit under test has a producer, the tree, and asked that its absence fail (the operator, the pc overseer, at the P4 dialog, 2026-10-10).
**Kept:** The absent-baseline arm is held by the pin on the dev host; no runner read it. The a11y upload has three path members and fails only when none matches. Whether the version still wants a pull-request comment with the new violations was put to the operator at this wrap's route-resolve card.
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-10-10T08-04-06Z-wrap/
